runs.name: National Energy Services Reunited Corp.; Nasdaq NESR, an oilfield-services provider in the Middle East and North Africa in two segments, Production Services and Drilling and Evaluation Services; a BVI blank-check company of 2017 that bought NPS and GES on 2018-06-06, SAPESCO 2020 and Action Energy service lines 2021; warrants exchanged for shares July 2025; no longer a foreign private issuer from 2026-01-01, its FY2025 annual report a 10-K, the earlier ones 20-Fs; Grant Thornton dismissed 2026-08-04 effective after the FY2026 audit; the 10-K names no rival, SLB, Halliburton and Weatherford read as a CONVENTION of the run

runs.entry: Price **$19.11** (2026-10-15 close, through `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **100,851,754**, one class (10-Q cover, 0001493152-26-036720, `Screens/cover_shares.py`; checked against the same 10-Q's balance sheet, issued equals outstanding, no treasury shares; no later 8-K or prospectus issues shares); cap **$1,927M**; net debt $99.6M at 2026-06-30, the $225.8M secured term loan due 2027-11-04 being refinanced. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury par curve, 30-year, 2026-10-15). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (0001493152-26-009139), the 20-Fs for FY2018 to FY2024 (FY2021 inside the FY2022 and FY2023 20-Fs), the two 2026 10-Qs, the proxy (0001493152-26-012394), the 2026 8-Ks; one figure cross-checked (2025 operating cash $264,242K, filed statement against `tools/run.py`). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A, 7 and 9A and the 20-Fs' matching items (the brief's departure), stated in the run file. Q1 IN (a regional oilfield-services contractor read off its figures; the tender question goes to Q2). **Q2 OUT** on the deciding part, Production Services (66% of 2021 to 2025 segment operating profit): a castle shown open on the evidence; one customer 49% of 2025 revenue (54% in 2024), most contracts "can be cancelled or renegotiated by our customers at any time", price named first among the factors of competition; the deciding part's revenue moved on the re-tender of that customer's Saudi fracturing work in 2021, 2022 and 2025, and back up in 2026; operating margin 2021 to 2025 4.9% against Halliburton 14.1%, SLB 15.7%, Weatherford 12.9%, 11.5% pre-tax on tangible capital against 25.4% to 40.3%; the field's durable players ordinary over the full cycle 2018 to 2025 (Halliburton 8.7% on revenue, SLB 2.9% after charges, Weatherford reorganized 2019). The 10-K and the 20-Fs name no rival; SLB, Halliburton and Weatherford read as a CONVENTION of the run, company-wide tagged figures (none reports Middle East profit), not cross-checked line by line; ADES, Arabian Drilling, ADNOC Drilling and the Chinese state service companies flagged as non-filers. Q3 to Q12 not reached. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged:** the restatement of 2020 and earlier (2020 net income $50.1M to $16.6M, equity before 2020 cut $50.4M, never allocated to 2018 or 2019; unrecorded payables in Saudi Arabia and the UAE); a material weakness for FY2022 to FY2024, executive officers having "failed to set an appropriate tone at the top", declared remediated in 2025; an SEC cease-and-desist order of 2024-08-28 with a $400,000 penalty; Nasdaq delisting effective 2023-04-28, later relisted; auditors: KPMG dismissed 2021, PwC resigned 2023 with no opinion issued, KPMG resigned its re-audit 2023, Grant Thornton dismissed 2026, PwC appointed for FY2027; the CEO's bonus pays on adjusted EBITDA. After the stop: payables and accruals $305.3M (2024-12-31) to $603.2M (2026-06-30), $116.2M of 2025's $264.2M operating cash and $181.5M of the first half of 2026's $204.8M, "more closely controlling timing of payments" in the 10-Q's words; retained earnings negative 2021 to 2023; goodwill $645M unchanged since 2021; no dividends or buybacks, shares 85.6M (2018) to 100.85M. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: owner cash five-year mean 2021 to 2025 all-equity $41.2M after all spending (seller-financed capex and IPM investments added, which `tools/run.py` misses) and $71.3M maintenance only (depreciation as the guess, central); the series changes sign, so by (b) no growth; value **about $6.53 to $12.03** a share all-equity against $19.11 (equity-only $3.73 to $9.23), the cases yielding 2.0% and 3.5% at the price, no case earning the floor; fair price **about $4.59 all-equity** ($3.52 equity-only beside); not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. Contamination declared by the analyst: a `Test Runs/` listing showing the HMH, NGS, NOV, OIS, SEI and USAC run files of 2026-10-16, none opened; SEI commit subjects and memory-index lines about the queue in the session context; none used. Commits 1bc2d9c3, e84a5163, 3cd0d36f, 21a982cc, four. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for NESR). Citations: the analyst's `check_cites.py` PASS (37 ids, 19 quoted fragments); the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` no phantom, no E-id and no slip among 11 tight pairs; the wider sweep's misses are filing quotations and, in the foundations paragraph, the framework's own phrase "a share is a business" quoted in the sentence that cites M1997-109, the id set after the row's own words, not after that phrase. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) rivals where the filer names none and the real rivals report only company-wide: how far a company-wide comparison may stand for a regional one; (2) Q7 (b) with every growth measure meaningless while (e) makes the maintenance case central: whether the all-spending no-growth case is a legitimate bottom (kept; on the maintenance case alone the fair price is $6.08); (3) no fallback in (a) when the only years before the window are known to be misstated; (4) a payables release flattering the base, (d) silent on it (shown removed beside: $2.29 to $7.79); (5) the template's Q4 balance-sheet reading in a file closed at Q2 has no home but AFTER THE STOP. Could not get: the rivals' Middle East profit, a full-cycle base for NESR, the tax note (no carryforward priced); the 20% interest tax shield a CONVENTION of the run.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT on the deciding part, Production Services: a castle shown open on the evidence; one customer 49% of revenue under contracts cancellable at any time, its Saudi fracturing work re-tendered in 2021, 2022 and 2025, price named first; operating margin 4.9% 2021 to 2025 against 12.9% to 15.7% at SLB, Halliburton and Weatherford (rivals a CONVENTION of the run, the 10-K naming none), the field ordinary over 2018 to 2025. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the 2020 and earlier restatement, the tone-at-the-top material weakness FY2022 to FY2024, an SEC cease-and-desist order of 2024, a 2023 delisting, four auditor changes; payables nearly doubled to $603.2M by mid-2026. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value about $6.53 to $12.03 a share all-equity against $19.11, fair about $4.59 all-equity ($3.52 equity-only), not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: company-wide rivals for a regional field; Q7 (b) against (e) when no growth is credited; no (a) fallback for misstated early years; a payables release under (d); the Q4 balance-sheet reading in a file closed at Q2.
